html:
The Jesuit Missions of Chiquitos are a group of mission towns in the eastern lowlands of Bolivia, founded by Jesuits among the Chiquitano peoples from 1691. Six of their churches became a World Heritage Site in 1990.

Like the reductions of Paraguay, the towns gathered Indigenous people around a church and plaza, with farms, workshops and schools. The Swiss Jesuit Martin Schmid designed several of the wooden churches, and taught the people to build organs and violins. The missions became famous for baroque music.

The Jesuits were expelled in 1767, but unlike many missions, the towns lived on. Thousands of musical scores were later found in the archives, and a festival of baroque music is now held there. They show the Jesuit legacy in the lowlands of Bolivia.
